problem_statement: The kellymilligan/codrops-oct-2021-final project is a single-page three.js / canvas-sketch WebGL lab: a fullscreen refractive-material scene (a glass body lit by an HDR environment, with bloom postprocessing) rendered onto a fullscreen canvas, plus a foreground chrome layer built into the self-contained output. The chrome carries an absolutely-positioned masthead frame (Halcyon Optics Lab eyebrow, Transmission Material Studio heading, intro, and two navigation links) and a dat.gui control panel whose rows retune the material and postprocessing in real time. On top of that chrome the studio hosts its own native control surface: a Material presets HUD — a labelled strip of preset chips (Clear Glass, Frosted Glass, Amber Resin, Diamond, Emerald) with a live readout line — that retunes the SAME MeshPhysicalMaterial the dat.gui panel drives and prints the applied optics. The two masthead links open real secondary studio pages (Specimen notes and Material reference) that share the same chrome and the same preset HUD. Restyle and wire this foreground control layer coherently: the preset strip must lay out fluidly (wrapping so it never overflows a 390px phone), read cleanly (legible chips over the dark canvas), appear on every studio page (home + both secondary pages), and its readout must update to the selected preset on click. The underlying WebGL scene — the canvas, the refractive material and its bindings, the HDR environment, the bloom pass, the orbit controls, the GLTF dragon body, and the canvas-sketch --build --inline build flow — must be preserved unchanged.
required_content: Present the Material presets HUD strip over the canvas on the home studio surface: a labelled row of preset chips (Clear Glass, Frosted Glass, Amber Resin, Diamond, Emerald) and a readout line, laid out so the row wraps and never overflows the viewport horizontally at 390px.

Wire the preset chips to the readout so that clicking a preset retunes the material AND updates the readout line to that preset (e.g. clicking Diamond shows 'Preset: Diamond · IOR 2.42'); the active chip is marked and the readout tracks the selected preset, not a frozen initial value.

Carry the preset HUD strip consistently across all three studio pages — the home lab (index.html) and both secondary pages (specimen.html Specimen notes and material.html Material reference) — so the control surface is present on every page of the studio, not just the home lab.
Keep the preset chips legible and uncollided over the dark canvas: chips must not overlap, shingle, or wash out into the background (no dark-on-dark text), and must stay inside the HUD panel.

Preserve the WebGL scene and the relabelled dat.gui panel: the canvas, the refractive MeshPhysicalMaterial and its GUI bindings (Light Transmission, Refractive Index, Optical Thickness, Bloom Response), the HDR environment map, the UnrealBloom pass, the OrbitControls, the GLTF dragon body, and the canvas-sketch --build --inline build flow must remain intact and runnable.

Use the repo's own source and build system only (entry.html chrome template + src/index.js + the two secondary studio pages); do not add dependencies, remote fonts/analytics, generated screenshots, remote replacement media, or iframe shortcuts.
design_constraints: Treat this as an implementation-continuous restyle/wiring of the existing WebGL lab's foreground control layer, not as a new landing page or a redesign of the 3D scene.

The studio chrome keeps the dark fullscreen-canvas aesthetic and a coherent amber-on-slate accent palette; the preset HUD sits over the canvas as a control surface, the masthead frame stays bottom-left.
Relabel dat.gui controls through .name() display text so the material property keys, ranges, and onChange bindings stay identical and the scene keeps rendering.
The preset HUD strip must lay out fluidly (wrapping chips) so it stays within desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile viewports with no horizontal overflow and no chip overlap or clipping.
The preset readout must reflect the currently selected preset after each click; the click must both retune the material and re-render the readout to the clicked preset.
state_constraints: desktop_home, tablet_home, and mobile_home verify the restyled masthead chrome and the Material presets HUD strip (fluidly wrapping, legible) across viewports; mobile_home and mobile_canvas_regression check the preset strip does not overflow a 390px viewport.
desktop_controls verifies the relabelled dat.gui control panel (Light Transmission, Refractive Index, Optical Thickness, Bloom Response) is present alongside the HUD.
desktop_preset_diamond clicks the Diamond preset chip and verifies the readout updates to the Diamond preset (IOR 2.42), changed from the Clear Glass readout on desktop_home.

desktop_specimen and desktop_material verify the preset HUD strip is carried onto both secondary studio pages (Specimen notes, Material reference); desktop_canvas_regression and mobile_canvas_regression protect the fullscreen WebGL canvas surface after the restyle.

change_completion: The Material presets HUD strip (Clear Glass / Frosted Glass / Amber Resin / Diamond / Emerald chips plus a readout line) is present over the canvas on the home studio surface.
Clicking a preset chip retunes the material and updates the readout line to the selected preset (the readout tracks the clicked preset rather than staying at the initial value).

The dat.gui control rows and postprocessing folder carry the human-readable optics labels (Light Transmission, Refractive Index, Optical Thickness, Bloom Response) and the document reads as the Halcyon Optics Lab studio.
design_consistency: The preset HUD strip is carried consistently across the home lab and both secondary studio pages so the control surface appears on every page of the studio.
The preset chips stay legible and uncollided over the dark canvas (no overlap, shingling, clipping, or dark-on-dark text) and the amber-on-slate accent palette is coherent.
regression: The WebGL canvas, refractive material, HDR environment, bloom pass, orbit controls, GLTF dragon body, and canvas-sketch build flow remain intact and runnable.
The relabelled dat.gui panel and the Halcyon Optics Lab studio brand appear on the page.
responsive: The Material presets HUD strip wraps and stays within the viewport at desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile widths with no horizontal overflow.
The fullscreen canvas surface remains present behind the restyled chrome at every viewport.

metadata.source_repo_kind: Single-page three.js / canvas-sketch WebGL lab: a fullscreen refractive-material scene (glass body, HDR environment, bloom postprocessing) on a canvas, with a foreground masthead frame, a dat.gui control panel, and a native Material presets HUD, built to a self-contained inlined output.
metadata.selected_repo_reason: Runnable interactive-canvas repo whose foreground control layer (masthead, dat.gui labels, and a native material-preset HUD carried across the studio pages) is a natural implementation-continuous restyle/wiring target where the fullscreen WebGL scene and the canvas-sketch build flow must be preserved.

author_notes: Slot slot_126 targets interactive_canvas / implementation_continuity / restyle / layout, hardened to L4 on the Halcyon Optics Lab Transmission Material Studio. The native lever is the studio's own Material presets HUD — a preset-chip strip with a live readout that retunes the same MeshPhysicalMaterial the dat.gui panel drives — placed over the fullscreen refractive-glass canvas (the canvas is position:absolute so it never adds to document scrollWidth; the normal-flow preset strip is the overflow host). Four orthogonal discriminators: the preset strip wraps fluidly so it never overflows a 390px phone (no_horizontal_overflow); the HUD is carried across the home lab and both manufactured secondary studio pages (dom_assertions cross-page); the HUD renders legibly and uncollided over the canvas (visual_regression); and clicking a preset chip updates the readout to the selected preset (interaction_assertions). entry.html, src/index.js, specimen.html and material.html are the leg-varying files; the WebGL getProgramInfoLog/getShaderInfoLog null-coercion shim and the runtime assets are identical infrastructure across all legs so the swiftshader headless build stays runtime-clean. The refractive material, HDR environment, bloom pass, orbit controls, GLTF dragon body, and the canvas-sketch --build --inline flow are preserved unchanged.
